title: Microelectrode recordings (MER) from deep brain stimulation surgery in Parkinson's disease (STN targeting, 14 patients)
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings (MER) from 14 patients with Parkinson's disease undergoing stereotactic deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery targeting the subthalamic nucleus. Up to three channels were recorded at successive depths, with each depth labelled as inside (STN-IN) or outside (STN-OUT) the nucleus by neurophysiologists and surgeons. Left and right trajectories are included. The data are unfiltered and were re-packaged losslessly into iEEG-BIDS from a public Zenodo release.
methods_description: Recordings were obtained during DBS surgery with the data files stored per depth, with up to three channels each. The release provides raw int16 signals with no filtering or processing. They were converted to BrainVision float32 files with BIDS sidecars, with no resampling or re-referencing. A related article describes MicroGuide (Alpha Omega) acquisition with tungsten microelectrodes, 200-6000 Hz band-pass and 12 kHz sampling.
